title: Half-Sunken Ship
description: A merchant vessel lists between jagged rocks, its hull split open by the tide. Barnacles coat every surface and seawater sloshes through the lower decks. The mast still flies a tattered pennant, snapping in the salt wind.

choices.label: Salvage the cargo hold
choices.description: Waterlogged timber still has value if you can haul it out.

outcomes.text: You wade through knee-deep brine and drag out armfuls of usable timber. The hold was well-packed.
The timber is salvageable, but a hidden eel nest gives one of your party a nasty shock as they reach between the crates.
A section of hull gives way as you climb inside. You scramble out with only a few planks before the whole cargo hold floods.

choices.label: Search the captain's quarters
choices.description: The captain's lockbox might still hold coin.

outcomes.text: The lockbox is rusted but intact. Inside: a pouch of salt-crusted coins and a tidal pearl tucked in velvet.
You find a modest stash of coin beneath the captain's bunk. The rest was already looted.
The floor collapses as you step inside. You crash through to the lower deck, soaked and bruised, clutching a few coins.

choices.label: Pry barnacles from the hull
choices.description: The thick crustacean shells have use in crafting.

outcomes.text: The shells come off in clean slabs. Excellent crafting material, and the work is oddly satisfying.
You harvest a decent haul, but a venomous sea-snail hidden among the barnacles stings your hand.
The barnacles shatter into useless fragments. At least some kelp sinew tangled in the hull is still usable.
